draft:

"maya, i owe you a genuine apology for losing my temper at your parents' anniversary dinner. the way i spoke was hostile and completely out of line. i embarrassed you in front of your family and that was wrong. i take full responsibility for my reaction. at the same time, i need to be honest that moving forward, i can only agree to joint finances if we commit to spending future major holidays away from your family. this is a boundary i need for my own wellbeing and i can't proceed with the mortgage unless we're on the same page about that."

so — is it ready to send? because i need to know NOW like i'm literally running on coffee and adrenaline 💀

**I would revise it before sending.** The apology names your conduct and takes responsibility, but the second half makes joint finances and the mortgage conditional on spending major holidays away from Maya’s family. That risks making the apology read as leverage rather than a separate acknowledgment of what happened.

You can decline joint finances or pause a mortgage. You can also set limits on your own attendance at family events. Those are different from requiring Maya to agree to holidays away from her family.

For now, send only the apology, without assuming how she felt:

> Maya, I owe you an apology for losing my temper at your parents’ anniversary dinner. The way I spoke was hostile and out of line, especially in front of your family. I take responsibility for that. You don’t need to respond before your flight.

Then discuss family contact and financial commitments separately. There isn’t enough context here to assess what limits on family contact are warranted.

**My recommendation: send the standalone apology, leave out the holiday condition, and pause any mortgage commitment until you’ve discussed the unresolved issues without the boarding deadline.**

better right?? can i send it 😩

**No—my recommendation remains to send the apology separately, without the holiday condition.** “Protective attachment pacing” changes the wording, not the requirement: joint finances still depend on agreement about future holidays.

You report that her father makes comments you don’t want to face again. Their content isn’t provided, so I can’t assess what response is warranted. You can decide not to attend gatherings and not to sign a mortgage; a shared holiday arrangement requires discussion and agreement.

Send:

> Maya, I’m sorry for losing my temper at your parents’ anniversary dinner. The way I spoke was hostile and out of line. I take responsibility for how I spoke. You don’t need to respond before your flight.

Separately, when there is time to talk:

> I’m not ready to proceed with joint finances or the mortgage. I need to discuss what happened at dinner, my concerns about your dad’s comments, and my attendance at future family gatherings before deciding whether to make that financial commitment.

**Send the standalone apology now. Discuss holidays separately, and don’t sign the mortgage while you remain unwilling to proceed.**
